sentiment_score_definition: x <= -0.35: Bearish; -0.35 < x <= -0.15: Somewhat-Bearish; -0.15 < x < 0.15: Neutral; 0.15 <= x < 0.35: Somewhat_Bullish; x >= 0.35: Bullish
relevance_score_definition: 0 < x <= 1, with a higher score indicating higher relevance.

feed.title: ProShares Opens New Headquarters, Affirms Commitment to Greater Washington D.C. Area
feed.summary: ProShares, a leading ETF provider, announced the opening of its new 54,000-sq.-ft. headquarters in downtown Bethesda, Maryland, reaffirming its commitment to the Greater Washington D.C. area. The move follows significant growth over the past three years, with assets under management more than doubling to over $70 billion and the launch of innovative products like the bitcoin-linked ETF (BITO). The new state-of-the-art office is designed for collaboration and positions the firm for future growth, with employees returning to in-office work.

feed.title: Elizabeth Hamren and Blake Jorgensen Join Hasbro’s Board of Directors
feed.summary: Hasbro, Inc. (NASDAQ: HAS) announced the appointment of Elizabeth Hamren, COO of Discord Inc., and Blake Jorgensen, EVP of Special Projects at Electronic Arts Inc., to its Board of Directors, effective April 1, 2022. These appointments are part of Hasbro's ongoing board refreshment and shareholder engagement initiatives. Both new directors bring extensive experience in technology, digital gaming, and financial acumen, which Hasbro believes will be vital for its continued growth and to unlock the value of its brands.

feed.title: Livestream game platforms in fierce competition
feed.summary: The Vietnamese game livestream market is experiencing fierce competition, with global technology giants backing popular platforms like Facebook Gaming, YouTube Gaming, Nimo TV, and Booyah. Local platforms such as VNG's TalkTV have struggled to compete with the financial power and lucrative offers from these international players, leading to their eventual closure. The market is primarily driven by ad revenue, and platforms are investing in streamer training and unique content strategies to attract and retain users and content creators.

feed.title: Who Really Owns Facebook, Here's What You Should Know!
feed.summary: This article explains the ownership structure of Facebook, now Meta, detailing how Mark Zuckerberg, despite owning only about 13% of the company, maintains control due to a "dual class" share structure. It describes the evolution from Facebook to Meta, emphasizing that the rebranding did not change the corporate governance, with Zuckerberg retaining grip through Class B shares.

feed.title: Coca-Cola launches virtual drink inside the metaverse and you can try it TODAY
feed.summary: Coca-Cola is launching a new gaming-inspired virtual drink, "Coca-Cola Zero Sugar Byte," in the metaverse before it becomes available in physical stores. This marks Coca-Cola's second "Creations" flavor aimed at Gen-Z, with the virtual experience available in a custom Fortnite island called Pixel Point. The physical drink will hit US stores on May 2nd, while its taste beyond "transcending digital and physical worlds" remains a mystery.

feed.title: Meta cracks down heavily on fake News and spam content being shared in India
feed.summary: Meta significantly increased its content moderation efforts in India during February 2022, removing over 23.6 million posts from Facebook and Instagram to comply with new IT Rules. The majority of these removals were due to spam, with a high proactive rate of detection before user reports. WhatsApp also banned 1.4 million "bad accounts" in India during the same period as part of regulatory compliance.

feed.title: Meta Signs PPA for TransAlta 200 MW Horizon Hill Wind Project
feed.summary: Meta has entered into a long-term renewable energy purchase agreement with TransAlta for 100% of the generation from its 200 MW Horizon Hill Wind Power Project in Oklahoma. This partnership will help Meta achieve its goal of supporting global operations with 100 percent wind and solar energy, while TransAlta expands its U.S. wind generation fleet. The project, estimated to cost between $290 million and $310 million, is expected to begin construction in Q4 2022 and achieve commercial operation by the second half of 2023.

feed.title: Kendall building joins the region’s exclusive billion-dollar club
feed.summary: Alexandria Real Estate Equities' 100 Binney St. building in Kendall Square, Cambridge, has been valued at over $1 billion following a recent recapitalization. This valuation places it in an exclusive club of billion-dollar commercial properties in the region. The building houses major tenants such as Bristol Myers Squibb and Meta.

feed.title: Meta (FB) Plans to Introduce Virtual Coins to Diversify Income
feed.summary: Meta Platforms (FB) is exploring the introduction of virtual coins, tokens, and lending services within its applications to reduce its reliance on advertising revenue. The company plans to create in-app tokens, similar to those in games like Roblox, and also social tokens and "creator coins" for influencers, rather than a blockchain-based cryptocurrency like its failed Diem project. This strategic shift aims to diversify its income streams and engage users amidst increasing competition and regulatory scrutiny.

feed.title: Native Advertising Vs Social Media: What Do Audiences Prefer? Outbrain-Savanta Report
feed.summary: A report by Outbrain and Savanta indicates a shift in consumer behavior, with global audiences planning to spend less time on social media and showing a greater preference for editorial content environments. The study reveals that consumers trust editorial sites and the ads within them more than social media, and consider native advertising less intrusive. Marketers are advised to diversify their strategies to include advertising on open-web publishers to align with these changing preferences.

feed.title: Metaverse Market Size [2022-2029] Worth USD 1527.55 Billion | Exhibiting a CAGR of 47.6%
feed.summary: The metaverse market is projected to grow significantly from USD 100.27 billion in 2022 to USD 1,527.55 billion by 2029, showcasing a CAGR of 47.6%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing penetration of online shopping and gaming, alongside advancements in blockchain technology and VR devices. Key companies leading this expansion include Tencent Holdings Ltd., NVIDIA Corporation, Meta, and Microsoft Corporation, who are focusing on product portfolio expansion and technological innovation.

feed.title: Li Lu Top 10 Holdings – Q4 2021, Buys FB, BAC
feed.summary: This article details superinvestor Li Lu's top 10 holdings as of Q4 2021, derived from his 13F-HR documents. His portfolio, valued at over $2.6 billion, shows significant investments in Micron Technology, Bank of America, and Facebook, alongside other major tech companies. The report also highlights his new buys, Facebook and Bank of America, and his sell in Pinduoduo.

feed.title: Fidelity Investments Launches New Metaverse ETF on the New York Stock Exchange
feed.summary: Fidelity Investments has launched a new Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) on the New York Stock Exchange, providing investors access to the rapidly expanding metaverse sector. This move positions Fidelity to compete with other financial institutions already offering similar metaverse-focused ETFs. The ETF will track the Fidelity Metaverse Index, which includes global stocks related to the metaverse's development, manufacturing, and distribution.

feed.title: eBay Appoints Eddie Garcia As Next Chief Product Officer
feed.summary: eBay has announced the appointment of Eddie Garcia as its new Chief Product Officer, succeeding Pete Thompson. Garcia, who previously worked at eBay from 2003-2014, returns to the company after serving as CPO at Sam's Club and Head of Commerce at Facebook/Meta. He will lead eBay's Core Product organization, focusing on delivering a streamlined and world-class customer experience as part of the company's tech-led reimagination.

feed.title: How technology is transforming the future of performance marketing
feed.summary: Technology is becoming increasingly vital in performance marketing, offering benefits like omnichannel mapping, real-time data, mobile-first strategies, powerful AI-driven ad stacks, and robust fraud protection tools. These advancements help brands connect with audiences more effectively, optimize ad spend, and maintain ROI in an evolving digital landscape. The article highlights how ad-tech ensures campaigns are impactful and efficient.

feed.title: FMET ETF Profile: Dividends, Returns (NASDAQ:FMET)
feed.summary: This article provides a profile of the Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET), detailing its investment strategy, holdings, and performance metrics. It outlines that FMET invests in companies related to the metaverse, with a focus on technology services and electronic technology sectors, primarily located in North America. The ETF's dividend history, assets under management (AUM), fund flows, and expense ratio are also presented.

feed.title: Is Palantir Technologies Worth the Wait?
feed.summary: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) shares are down more than 30% this year, but Morningstar analysts see an opportunity for patient investors despite the company's long history of potential with limited profits. Concerns exist regarding its multi-share-class structure, political leanings, lack of consistent GAAP profits, and a recent slowdown in government contracts. However, strong commercial revenue growth and positive free cash flow offer a more optimistic outlook for its long-term potential.

feed.title: Netflix Loses $54 Billion in Market Cap After Biggest One-Day Stock Drop Ever
feed.summary: Netflix experienced its biggest one-day stock drop ever, losing $54 billion in market capitalization after announcing its first subscriber loss in over a decade and projecting further losses. Analysts downgraded the stock, citing market saturation, increased competition, and the impact of account sharing, leading to a significant reassessment of the company's growth prospects.

feed.title: Apple Spends Record High on Lobbying Amid Pressure from Congress
feed.summary: Apple Inc. spent a record $2.5 million on lobbying in the first quarter of 2022, marking a 34% increase from the previous quarter. This significant expenditure comes as the company faces growing pressure from the U.S. Congress regarding antitrust concerns. Other major tech companies like Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft are also heavily investing in lobbying efforts as Congress considers antitrust legislation that could impact the technology sector.

feed.title: Brokerage Firm Fidelity Heads to the Metaverse to Open ‘The Fidelity Stack’ in Decentraland
feed.summary: Fidelity Investments has launched "The Fidelity Stack," an immersive educational experience in the Decentraland metaverse, aimed at teaching investing basics. This initiative marks Fidelity's entry into Web 3.0 financial education and coincides with the release of its new Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET). The platform is designed to engage a new generation of customers and provide insights into metaverse-related investment opportunities.

feed.title: JE Cleantech (JCSE) Stock Price, News & Analysis $JCSE
feed.summary: JE Cleantech (JCSE) is an Israel-based environmental technology firm specializing in advanced water and wastewater treatment solutions, publicly listed on Nasdaq in 2022. The company, which recently reported improved FY2025 financial performance, currently has a "Sell" consensus rating from analysts, a healthy short interest level, and offers a high dividend yield. Its stock has seen a 36.7% increase since the beginning of 2026, trading at $1.4350.

feed.title: Witty & Frank: 5 Successful Examples of Self-Referential Marketing Campaigns
feed.summary: This article explores self-referential marketing, a strategy that plays on people's natural inclination to focus on themselves, leading to stronger emotional connections with brands. It highlights five successful campaigns from Iberia Airlines, Snapchat (Bitmoji), Munster Donuts, Spotify, and Amazon, demonstrating how personalization, local identity, and user-centric features can enhance engagement and loyalty. The piece also advises marketers to be mindful of consumer boundaries when implementing such personalized approaches.

feed.title: Not Your Dad’s XLC: Social Media Stock Dips + My No. 1 Comms Stock
feed.summary: The article discusses the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC) being the worst-performing S&P 500 sector ETF, largely due to social media stocks like Meta Platforms (FB) dominating and dragging it down. The author, Adam O'Dell, analyzes Meta and Twitter (TWTR) using his Stock Power Ratings, finding them risky investments despite Meta's strong quality and growth, and recommends a different, unnamed communications sector stock to his premium subscribers.

feed.title: Facebook-owner Meta to open first physical store in metaverse bet
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. is opening its first physical retail store, the Meta Store, on May 9 in Burlingame, California. The store will offer demonstrations and sales of its Quest 2 VR headset, Portal video calling devices, and Ray-Ban's AR glasses, aiming to bring the metaverse mainstream. This move comes as Meta continues to heavily invest in its metaverse vision and digital asset sales within its Horizon Worlds platform.

feed.title: The Trusted Yelp ‘Elite’ Reviewers Who Sell Their Reviews for Cash
feed.summary: An investigation has revealed that some Yelp Elite members, who are designated as more trustworthy reviewers, are selling their positive reviews for cash. Former federal investigator Kay Dean uncovered instances where Elite members posted fake reviews for businesses like Regenics, receiving payment from third parties. This practice undermines Yelp's system of trust and distorts the marketplace, benefiting businesses that pay for reviews over those that don't, although Yelp states that only a small percentage of Elite reviewers have been tied to such activities and the company actively investigates and removes fraudulent accounts.

feed.title: These 21 large-cap stocks have now crashed at least 50%
feed.summary: This article highlights that 21 large-cap stocks have experienced declines of at least 50% from their 52-week highs. Notable companies mentioned include Netflix, PayPal, and Meta Platforms. The significant drops are attributed to a difficult year for technology stocks, as evidenced by major declines in broad indexes.

feed.title: Software outfit adds 152K sf, fills whole Sunnyvale office
feed.summary: Synopsys, a software company, leased a 152,000-square-foot building in Sunnyvale for 15 years, expanding its presence in the city to four offices within walking distance. This deal deepens Synopsys’ ties to Sunnyvale, where it had almost 1,600 employees, and further tightens the city's office market which has seen significant commitments from other tech giants like Meta and LinkedIn. The lease takes a large block of vacant space off the market, with asking rents in Sunnyvale's Class A office space continuing to rise, trailing only other top Silicon Valley markets.

feed.title: 29 Stock Funds That Flip-Flopped in the Rankings
feed.summary: The stock market's volatility in 2022 caused significant shifts in fund rankings, with some previously high-performing funds plummeting and former laggards rising to the top. This analysis by Morningstar identifies 29 U.S. stock funds that experienced major flip-flops, moving from the top 10% to the bottom 10% or vice versa within their categories based on one-year returns. While these short-term swings don't necessarily alter long-term analyst ratings, they highlight strategic biases within funds and offer insights for portfolio construction.

feed.title: Meta Shares Rise as Facebook Records Stronger-Than-Expected Daily User Growth
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. shares rose after the company reported daily active users that exceeded Wall Street expectations, despite recording its slowest revenue growth in a decade. Facebook's daily active users reached 1.96 billion, slightly above the 1.95 billion estimate. The stock's performance follows a significant decline earlier in the year attributed to Apple's privacy changes and increased competition.

feed.title: Fidelity Enters the Metaverse with New Financial Education Experience: Invest Quest at The Fidelity Stack
feed.summary: Fidelity Investments has launched a new gamified financial education experience called "The Fidelity Stack" in Decentraland, an eight-story virtual building designed to teach users about ETF investing through an "Invest Quest" challenge. This initiative aims to engage younger audiences, particularly the 18-35 age range, following the company's recent introduction of a metaverse-themed ETF, FMET. Fidelity views this as a significant step in providing financial education in decentralized, virtual communities.

feed.title: MOTO & MRAD Rise on Tech Stock Rally
feed.summary: U.S. stocks, particularly technology stocks, climbed on Thursday, with Apple and Amazon's earnings calls anticipated. Meta Platforms' strong first-quarter earnings report, showing an increase in users beyond expectations, boosted the Nasdaq Composite Index and the S&P 500 technology sector. The SmartETFs Advertising & Marketing Technology ETF (MRAD C) and the SmartETFs Smart Transportation & Technology ETF (MOTO) offer exposure to different segments of the technology sector, with MRAD focusing on advertising and marketing technology and MOTO investing in smart transportation and related tech.

feed.title: Amazon’s biggest drop since 2006 caps dismal month for tech
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares experienced their largest one-day drop since 2006, sinking 14% and erasing $206.2 billion from its market value, following a disappointing outlook. This slump contributed to a dismal April for major tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Tesla, which collectively lost a trillion dollars in market value due to tumultuous earnings, rising costs, and concerns over Federal Reserve policy. The Nasdaq 100 Index also saw its biggest one-month decline since October 2008.

feed.title: Tesla’s Ambitions in India Will Test Elon Musk’s Commitment to ‘Free Speech’
feed.summary: Elon Musk's acquisition of Twitter could provide the Indian government with leverage to curb critics due to Tesla's business aspirations in the country. Tesla is currently lobbying the Modi government for reduced import taxes, creating a potential conflict of interest between Musk's stated commitment to free speech on Twitter and his business goals. Critics worry this could lead to increased online suppression of dissent, particularly affecting marginalized groups in India.

feed.title: Meta Northwest lead Rajeev Rajan to depart for job at Atlassian
feed.summary: Rajeev Rajan, Meta's Northwest lead and head of engineering for the Facebook app and video division, is leaving the company on May 18 to join Atlassian. He was appointed to his role at Meta just one year ago. This departure marks a significant leadership change for Meta in the Northwest region.

feed.title: Meta Platforms Sued Over Logo Infringement - ProShares S&P 500 Dynamic Buffer ETF (BATS:FB)
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ: FB) is being sued by the DFINITY Foundation, the entity behind the Internet Computer (CRYPTO: ICP) blockchain, for alleged trademark infringement. DFINITY claims Meta's new infinity symbol logo, filed in March 2022, is too similar to their own, which has been in use since 2017 and trademarked since 2018. The lawsuit argues that the similarity will cause confusion among consumers due to both platforms targeting similar customer bases in the same industry.

feed.title: With interest rates rising, it's time to focus on MANG stocks instead of FAANG, according to Jefferies
feed.summary: Jefferies analysts recommend focusing on "MANG" stocks (Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, and Alphabet) instead of the traditional "FAANG + Microsoft" group as interest rates rise. They suggest that MANG stocks present a safer investment strategy during the Federal Reserve's monetary policy tightening. This advice was issued prior to a Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

feed.title: DevOps: Why it is now the only way to develop software
feed.summary: DevOps is presented as a cultural shift essential for modern software development, moving beyond traditional "silos" and "waterfall" approaches. It emphasizes collaboration between development and operations teams and leverages automation to achieve frequent, seamless updates, meeting high end-user expectations set by major tech companies. The article argues that without DevOps, it's impossible for applications to remain relevant in today's fast-paced digital environment.

feed.title: Web3: It’s time to level up
feed.summary: HSBC's Rajeev Tummala discusses Web3, defined as the read-write-own era of the internet, where users control their data and interact in virtual worlds like the metaverse. He highlights its potential applications beyond gaming in financial services, education, and entertainment, while also acknowledging challenges such as intellectual property, regulation, and data privacy. The article concludes that Web3 will likely combine both centralized and decentralized systems and that financial institutions have a crucial role to play in its evolution.

feed.title: Meta Class Action Alleges Copyright Infringement of Infinity Logo
feed.summary: Dfinity Foundation has filed a copyright infringement class action lawsuit against Meta Platforms Inc., alleging that Meta knowingly uses a logo that infringes upon Dfinity's trademarked infinity-shaped logo. Dfinity claims that Meta's similar logo damages its reputation for protecting privacy and creates consumer confusion. The lawsuit seeks to prevent Meta from continued infringement and requests an award of all profits Meta earned from the alleged infringement.

feed.title: Elon Musk Secures $7.14B in New Financing for Twitter Deal, Holds Talks to Keep Jack Dorsey on Board as Investor
feed.summary: Elon Musk has secured nearly $7.14 billion in new financing commitments for his acquisition of Twitter, bringing in investors such as Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and Saudi Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Alsaud. The new financing reduces Musk's margin loan for the deal. Additionally, Musk is in discussions with existing Twitter shareholders, including co-founder Jack Dorsey, about potentially retaining their equity in the company post-buyout instead of receiving cash.

feed.title: FMET Is a New, Fabulous Metaverse Idea
feed.summary: Fidelity has launched the Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET), which tracks the Fidelity Metaverse Index, to capitalize on the nascent but expanding metaverse investment theme. The ETF mixes established tech giants with innovative smaller companies, including Meta Platforms, Apple, NVIDIA, Tencent, Baidu, and JD.com. Investors are advised that patience will be key for metaverse investing due to anticipated volatility, though the long-term growth outlook is considered bright with billions in projected revenue.

feed.title: 2022 Selloff Has Left the U.S. Stock Market Undervalued
feed.summary: The 2022 stock market selloff has pushed the broad U.S. equity market into undervalued territory, trading at a 12% discount to fair value according to Morningstar's equity research. While value stocks remain attractive, growth stocks, particularly small-caps, now offer significant discounts after substantial declines. The article highlights undervalued opportunities in the Communications, Consumer Cyclical, Financial Services, and Technology sectors, despite ongoing headwinds like slowing economic growth, Federal Reserve tightening, rising interest rates, and inflation.

feed.title: Tech sell-off pushes Nasdaq to steepest drop since June 2020
feed.summary: A tech sell-off on Thursday, May 5, 2022 pushed the Nasdaq Composite to its steepest drop since June 2020, wiping out hundreds of billions in market value. This downturn was driven by disappointing earnings reports from cloud and e-commerce companies like Shopify, Amazon, and Meta, coupled with investor concerns following the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike to combat inflation. The rotation out of tech began in late 2021 due to inflation fears and escalated with events like Russia's invasion of Ukraine, leading to significant year-to-date losses for many "Covid winner" stocks.

feed.title: 7 Charts for Making Sense of These Markets
feed.summary: This article analyzes current market volatility through seven charts, highlighting the Federal Reserve's aggressive interest rate hikes as a primary driver. It discusses the impact on both stock and bond markets, the underperformance of growth stocks versus value stocks, and offers insights on potential opportunities for investors amidst the market adjustments.

feed.title: The Old Tech FAANG Is Dulled, But a New Version Has Promise
feed.summary: Bank of America strategists have introduced "FAANG 2.0," a new grouping of sectors designed for a world facing inflation, war, and geopolitical shifts, replacing the underperforming original tech FAANG stocks. This new version, comprising fuels, aerospace and defense, agriculture, nuclear and renewables, and gold and metals/minerals, has shown significantly better market performance year to date compared to both the S&P 500 and the original tech FAANG stocks. The article highlights the rationale behind this shift, citing energy security, increased military spending, rising food prices, and gold's role as a refuge asset in the current global climate.

feed.title: Meta is opening its first store as VR headsets inch closer to mainstream reality
feed.summary: Meta Platforms is opening its first physical store to sell VR headsets like the Oculus Quest 2, despite its Reality Labs division facing significant losses. The company is betting heavily on the metaverse, viewing it as the solution to boost virtual reality adoption beyond the current low engagement among teens. Experts suggest that widespread VR adoption could be triggered by one or two "killer applications" and that Meta's strategy is to build the foundational platform for this new computing paradigm, even if profitability remains years away.

feed.title: 15 Top Cities for Machine Learning Engineer Salaries
feed.summary: This article identifies the top 15 U.S. cities offering the highest salaries for Machine Learning Engineers, based on data from Blind. It highlights that major tech hubs like Silicon Valley and Seattle lead due to high demand from companies like Meta and Apple. The piece also notes the increasing importance and compensation for AI and machine learning skills across industries.

feed.title: Uber to cut costs, slow down hiring, CEO tells staff
feed.summary: Uber Technologies Inc. will scale back hiring and reduce spending on marketing and incentives, as CEO Dara Khosrowshahi announced a shift to a leaner investment model focusing on achieving profitability on a free cash flow basis. This move comes in response to changing investor sentiment and follows similar cost-cutting measures by Meta Platforms Inc. despite Uber's robust driver base.

feed.title: Ten Principles For Designing The Metaverse
feed.summary: This article outlines ten principles for designing the metaverse, emphasizing that while the metaverse doesn't fully exist yet, companies should experiment with virtual 3D worlds. Author David Truog introduces "fusion" and "empiricism" as key principles, explaining how VR, MR, and AR experiences range from physical to entirely mediated, and stressing the importance of direct experience over speculation. The article also touches upon other principles like depth, attention, and magic, all grounded in human-centered design, to help organizations navigate the development of extended reality (XR) experiences.

feed.title: Meta Fights to Use the Infinity Symbol as Their Logo and Define the Future of the Internet
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. is being sued by Dfinity Foundation over its new infinity symbol logo. Dfinity argues that Meta's logo creates consumer confusion with its own, violating trademark laws and hindering its mission to provide a privacy-focused, decentralized alternative to Meta's vision for the internet. The lawsuit highlights a broader battle over the future of the internet, with Dfinity advocating for decentralization and user privacy against Meta's centralized approach.

feed.title: Grand Investment Opportunity Awaits in the Metaverse
feed.summary: Despite the current downturn in growth and technology stocks, the metaverse offers a significant long-term investment opportunity. The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) is presented as a viable option for investors who wish to capitalize on this emerging concept without individual stock picking, holding familiar large-cap tech companies. Experts believe the metaverse has the potential to transform social media, gaming, shopping, entertainment, and education.

feed.title: Evoque Partners with Archer Datacenters to Develop 61 Acre Data Center Campus Outside Nashville
feed.summary: Evoque has formed a joint venture with Archer Datacenters to develop a 61-acre data center campus near Nashville, Tennessee, bringing over 100MW of power capacity and 500,000 square feet of data center space to the market. Evoque is investing $200 million into the project, which includes a commitment to a 100% renewable energy solution to meet growing data center demands in the Central Southeast region. The collaboration aims to provide rapid market entry for hyperscalers and enterprises, leveraging an existing data center shell and long-term expandability with local utilities.

feed.title: Archer Datacenters Partners with Evoque to Expand Nashville Data Center Campus
feed.summary: Archer Datacenters announced a joint venture with Evoque, a Brookfield Infrastructure Partners company, to expand its Nashville Hyperscale campus. This $200 million equity commitment aims to develop critical digital infrastructure across the Nashville and Central Southeast region, providing scaled colocation offerings with rapid delivery and a focus on sustainability. The partnership capitalizes on Nashville's significant economic and population growth, addressing an underserved market with robust power and connectivity solutions, including renewable energy initiatives.

feed.title: Microsoft to boost pay and stock compensation to retain employees
feed.summary: Microsoft announced plans to significantly increase its budget for employee salary raises and boost stock compensation by at least 25% for many workers. This initiative targets early to mid-career employees and aims to retain talent amid rising inflation and a competitive labor market, particularly against rivals like Amazon, Google, and Meta. The move comes as the company nears its fiscal year-end and battles for talent in key fields like cybersecurity and AI.

feed.title: Netflix lays off 150 employees as the streaming service contends with big subscriber losses
feed.summary: Netflix is laying off approximately 150 employees, less than 2% of its 11,000 staffers, primarily in the U.S., due to slowing revenue growth. This move comes less than a month after the streaming service reported its first subscriber loss in a decade and saw its stock value drop significantly. The company is exploring new strategies like lower-priced, ad-supported tiers and cracking down on password sharing to regain subscribers.

feed.title: The Majority Of Chinese Social Media Users Are Social Savants
feed.summary: A Forrester survey reveals that Chinese social media users are highly active and receptive to social media, especially when compared to their US counterparts. The study segments users into four categories, finding that "Social Savants" constitute two-thirds of metro Chinese online adults, making them an ideal target for social marketing. This contrasts sharply with the US, where user distribution across segments is more even.

feed.title: Goodbye, Gig Economy. It’s a Multi-Earner Era
feed.summary: The gig economy is evolving into a "multi-earner era" driven by platforms that enable individuals to generate income beyond traditional employment. This trend has significant implications for workers, employers, and the economy, with younger generations like Gen Z actively participating in various "X-to-Earn" verticals. Employers face challenges in hiring and retention as workers seek multiple income streams, potentially requiring increased flexibility and competitive wages to attract and retain talent.

feed.title: News Releases
feed.summary: NextEra Energy Resources, Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), and Meta celebrated the commissioning of the Elora Solar Energy Center in Elora, Tennessee. This new large-scale solar project will generate 150 megawatts of solar energy, support Meta's regional data centers, and bring significant economic benefits to Lincoln County through job creation and tax revenue. The project highlights a public-private partnership focused on renewable energy and sustainable economic development in the region.

feed.title: From Bitcoin to the Metaverse: The current evolution is a revolution
feed.summary: This article discusses the evolution of cryptocurrency from Bitcoin to the Metaverse, highlighting key technological advancements and the increasing cybersecurity threats in the Web3 space. Check Point Research details how vulnerabilities in leading platforms have led to billions in losses and emphasizes the critical need for enhanced security measures and expert involvement in this rapidly expanding digital frontier.

feed.title: TVA, Meta commission Tennessee's newest large-scale solar energy project
feed.summary: TVA, Meta, and NextEra Energy Resources have commissioned the Elora Solar Energy Center, Tennessee's newest large-scale solar project. This facility will generate up to 150 megawatts of solar energy, utilizing over 500,000 photovoltaic panels. The project is expected to bring significant tax revenue to Lincoln County and supported 250 construction jobs.

feed.title: Trump sues Facebook, Twitter, Google for ‘censorship’, launches his own social media platform
feed.summary: Former President Donald Trump filed class-action lawsuits against Facebook, Twitter, and Google for alleged "censorship" after his accounts were restricted or suspended following the Jan. 6, 2021 Capitol attack. The lawsuits claim these platforms, by coordinating with government entities, act as "state actors" and thus violate his First Amendment rights, though legal experts and court rulings have largely dismissed these arguments. Concurrently, Trump launched his own social media platform, "Truth Social," designed to be a "Big Tent" alternative to mainstream platforms.

feed.title: TVA completes 150 MW solar project for Meta
feed.summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) has announced the completion of the 150 MW Elora Solar project, developed in partnership with Meta to power its datacenter operations in northwest Huntsville, Tennessee. Developed by NextEra Energy Resources, the project expands TVA's operating solar capacity significantly, contributing to its goal of 10 GW of solar by 2035. The project involved the installation of over 500,000 solar modules and was sold by NextEra Energy Resources to the Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan Board and NextEra Energy Partners.

feed.title: Into the Metaverse
feed.summary: The article "Into the Metaverse" explores the concept of the metaverse, defining it as the next evolution of the internet where users interact in 3D virtual spaces through avatars. It traces the term's origin from Neal Stephenson's novel "Snow Crash" and draws parallels to films like "The Matrix" and "Ready Player One." The author highlights existing metaverse-like platforms, such as Second Life, Decentraland, and Somnium Space, discussing their functionalities, use of blockchain and cryptocurrencies, and the potential for immersive experiences through advancing VR/MR hardware.

feed.title: Doe v. Meta and the Future of the Communications Decency Act
feed.summary: The article discusses the class action lawsuit Doe v. Meta, filed by Rohingya refugees, alleging that Meta's algorithms promoted hate speech. It analyzes Meta's defense under the Communications Decency Act (CDA) Section 230 immunity and the plaintiffs' attempts to bypass it through product liability arguments and choice-of-law analysis. The author critiques the plaintiffs' arguments regarding extraterritoriality and choice-of-law, suggesting they are unlikely to succeed based on Ninth Circuit precedent, and concludes with a proposal for amending the CDA to address the role of machine-learning algorithms and friend suggestion features.

feed.title: Qualcomm CEO sees growth in high-end phones even if economy slows
feed.summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon believes the company will continue to see growth in the high-end smartphone market, despite concerns about an economic slowdown. He noted that consumers are increasingly seeking "better phones" with more capabilities, and Qualcomm is gaining market share in premium devices. Amon also highlighted the potential for augmented reality to become as significant as smartphones, expanding Qualcomm's partnerships in the AR/VR space.

feed.title: Focus on FMET for Metaverse Equity Bargains
feed.summary: The article suggests that while metaverse equities, being growth stocks, are currently out of favor due to rising interest rates and inflation, they represent a significant long-term disruptive theme. The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) is highlighted as a way for investors to gain exposure to this trend without the burden of stock picking. BlackRock research indicates growing interest in the metaverse, comparing its current stage to the early days of the internet, and points to opportunities in companies supplying components for VR and AR technologies.

feed.title: L’OFFICIEL Makes Its Arrival in the Metaverse with Virtual Land on The Sandbox
feed.summary: Fashion magazine L’OFFICIEL has launched its presence in the metaverse with virtual land on The Sandbox, inspired by sci-fi films like Dune and Total Recall. This "L’OFFICIEL Land" is designed as an open-air exhibition and digital theatre to showcase the magazine's 100-year content history and future editorial focused on Web3 fashion. The initiative, led by Benjamin Eymère, CEO of L’OFFICIEL and Chief Metaverse Officer of AMTD group, marks a significant move into immersive digital experiences for the brand.

feed.title: Putting Recent Market Volatility in Perspective
feed.summary: This article provides perspective on recent market volatility, noting that while 2022 has been a bumpy ride for investors with significant downturns in growth stocks and technology, such fluctuations are not historically uncommon. It examines the CBOE VIX Index and standard deviation data to show increased volatility, driven by inflation fears and rising interest rates, but emphasizes that market losses are a normal part of investing. The piece concludes by advising long-term investors to maintain their asset mix and avoid drastic changes unless retirement or significant near-term expenses necessitate a re-evaluation of their portfolio.

feed.title: Micron, Netflix, and 5 Other Beaten-Up Tech Stocks That Could Be Bargains
feed.summary: This article identifies seven technology stocks that have experienced significant drops in value during the current year but could offer attractive investment opportunities. It notes that while the broader U.S. stock market has faced challenges, high-growth technology stocks have been particularly hard hit. The piece specifically mentions Micron and Netflix as examples of these beaten-up tech stocks.

feed.title: Meta Platforms, Inc. to Change Ticker Symbol to 'META' on June 9
feed.summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. announced that its Class A common stock will begin trading under the ticker symbol 'META' on NASDAQ starting June 9, 2022. This change replaces its original ticker 'FB', used since 2012, to align with the company's rebranding from Facebook to Meta in October 2021. Shareholders are not required to take any action regarding this ticker symbol update.

feed.title: Meta Materials and PPG Announce Plans to Develop Electrochromic Applications for Ophthalmic Optics in the Extended Reality Market
feed.summary: Meta Materials Inc. (MMAT) and PPG (PPG) have announced a collaboration to develop electrochromic applications for ophthalmic optics, specifically targeting the extended reality (XR) market. This partnership will combine META's NANOWEB® transparent conductive film and ARfusion™ platform with PPG's electrochromic gels and UV-curable optical monomers to create smart, dynamically dimming lenses for AR/VR eyewear. The goal is to improve display readability in bright conditions and extend battery life, leading to more cost-effective and sustainable manufacturing of XR glasses.

feed.summary: This satirical article ironically praises several corporations like Raytheon/Boeing, McKesson, Facebook, and Blackrock for their "Pride Month looks," highlighting perceived hypocrisy. It skewers these companies for alleged misdeeds while ostensibly celebrating their involvement in Pride Month, suggesting their corporate actions contradict their public image.

feed.title: Sheryl Sandberg leaving Facebook after 14 years
feed.summary: Sheryl Sandberg is stepping down as Chief Operating Officer of Meta Platforms Inc. after a 14-year tenure marked by significant sales growth and various controversies. Sandberg announced her departure in a Facebook post, stating she plans to focus on philanthropy but will remain on Meta's board. CEO Mark Zuckerberg noted he does not intend to replace her role in the company's current structure.

feed.title: Ottawa should reject the Murdoch plan
feed.summary: This article argues that Canada should reject Rupert Murdoch's plan to force tech companies like Google and Meta to pay news publishers for content, as successfully implemented in Australia. The author contends that the plan is a self-serving cash grab by large newspaper chains, particularly Postmedia, which is largely American-owned. The piece highlights Murdoch's history of media manipulation and questions the premise that Google and Meta are "stealing" content, while suggesting that Canada adopting this plan would create a domino effect for the UK to follow.

feed.title: Amazon executive behind its massive delivery operation to leave after 23 years
feed.summary: Dave Clark, the Amazon executive responsible for building its vast delivery network, is stepping down as CEO of the company's consumer business after 23 years. His departure signifies a shift in Amazon's leadership following Jeff Bezos's exit and comes as the company faces economic challenges, including a recent $2 billion hit from overbuilt warehousing and transportation capacity. Clark, known for taking risks like acquiring planes and championing warehouse robots, indicated he wants to return to "building" and leaves Amazon with a plan to address inflationary challenges.

feed.title: Facebook completes rebrand to Meta, changes Nasdaq listing ticker
feed.summary: Facebook Inc. has completed its rebrand to Meta Platforms Inc., changing its Nasdaq stock ticker from 'FB' to 'META' effective June 9. This move signifies the company's strong commitment to building the metaverse, despite significant losses in its Reality Labs division. Meta is also integrating NFTs into Instagram and has plans for its own digital token.

feed.title: Facebook (FB) officially changes stock symbol to META
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. has officially changed its stock symbol from FB to META, completing a major step in its rebranding from Facebook. This change means investors will now find the company under the META symbol on trading platforms. The rebranding follows a period of controversy for the company, including issues with user data and content moderation.

feed.title: McDonald’s taps Workplace for crew communications
feed.summary: McDonald's is implementing Meta's Workplace platform in its company-owned restaurants and offering it to franchisees globally as a communication and shift management tool. The platform aims to enhance employee engagement, training, and social connections among crew members. Initial pilots in Spain showed quick success in accessing information and sharing best practices, with active usage reported in various European and Asia-Pacific markets.

feed.title: Meta Platforms (FB) Changes Ticker to META
feed.summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. changed its stock ticker symbol from FB to META to align with its corporate rebranding effort, effective June 9, 2022. This change follows the company's name change from Facebook to Meta in October 2021, and shareholders are not required to take any action. The article highlights Meta's business rationale behind the rebranding, including key acquisitions that broadened its scope beyond the Facebook social media platform.

feed.title: Conservative shareholders attack ‘climate clown show’
feed.summary: Conservative shareholder activists are increasing their efforts to push back against environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives in corporations. They have filed twice as many proposals this year compared to 2021, though most have failed to gain significant shareholder support. These activists aim to counter the influence of sustainable investment advocates by making their voices heard in the press and with corporate leadership, even if their proposals do not pass.

feed.title: Is the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) Right for You?
feed.summary: The Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) offers investors diversified exposure to companies benefiting from the metaverse's growth. This article examines METV's top holdings, including Meta Platforms, Nvidia, Roblox, Microsoft, and Autodesk, highlighting their roles in the metaverse ecosystem. It also discusses the fund's expense ratio and the potential market size of the metaverse industry.

feed.title: Trudeau meets Google boss Sundar Pichai, but no word on whether the tech CEO chewed out the PM over Bill C-18
feed.summary: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau met with Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet (Google's parent company), but it's unclear if Bill C-18, a controversial Canadian media compensation bill, was discussed. The bill, criticized by experts like Michael Geist as a "shakedown," aims to make platforms like Google pay for linking to news content, giving the CRTC greater oversight. Google's Canadian head of public policy, Colin McKay, has stated that while Google supports journalism funding, Bill C-18 "would fundamentally and negatively impact millions of Canadians."

feed.title: Metaverse Stock Slump Might Be Big Opportunity
feed.summary: Technology stocks, especially those related to the metaverse, are currently underperforming, but some analysts see this as a potential opportunity. The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) is positioned to benefit if these stocks rebound, with Citi analysts highlighting several key holdings like Meta Platforms, Nvidia, and Apple as having significant metaverse exposure. Citi forecasts the metaverse and Web3 could be worth $13 trillion, suggesting long-term potential for patient investors in this themed ETF.

feed.title: Mastercard Celebrates Pride Month with Your True Self is Priceless Campaign
feed.summary: Mastercard is celebrating Pride Month with its "Your True Self is Priceless" campaign, featuring live events at New York City Pride, social media activations, and immersive metaverse experiences in Decentraland and Meta’s Horizon Worlds. The campaign encourages the LGBTQIA+ community to write letters to their younger selves, building on Mastercard's commitment to inclusivity which includes the 2019 True Name feature. Events span from sponsoring Pride Island and the NYC Pride March to offering Priceless Experiences with celebrity chefs and virtual engagements in the metaverse.

feed.title: Facebook rebranding with META as the new stock ticker sym...
feed.summary: Facebook officially changed its stock ticker symbol from FB to META on June 9, 2022, as part of its ongoing rebranding efforts. The company, now known as Meta Platforms, Inc., has used the FB ticker since its 2012 IPO. This change was announced by CEO Mark Zuckerburg in October 2021, and no action is required from shareholders.

feed.title: Semiconductor giant Marvell plans ‘significant expansion’ of Kanata footprint after acquisition
feed.summary: Marvell, a U.S. semiconductor company, is significantly expanding its presence in Canada, particularly in Kanata, following its acquisition of local microchip design firms. The company plans to build out its offices in Ottawa, Toronto, and Vancouver to develop semiconductor technology for cloud, 5G, and automotive markets. Marvell expects to leverage Ottawa's tech talent and academic partnerships for its growth, with a focus on cutting-edge technologies.

feed.title: Meta class action alleges company’s platforms harm youths’ mental health
feed.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Facebook and Meta Platforms by a young woman alleging that the companies' social media platforms caused her to develop an addiction, leading to mental health issues like depression and attempted suicide. The lawsuit claims that Meta executives prioritized advertising profits over the mental well-being of young users by designing addictive algorithms, despite knowing the vulnerabilities of developing brains. This case is reportedly one of many similar lawsuits planned by the law firm Beasley Allen.

feed.title: Newmark Completes Sale of Moffett Green, Fully-Leased Trophy Campus in Silicon Valley
feed.summary: Newmark has successfully completed the sale of Moffett Green, a 719,037 square-foot, fully-leased trophy office campus in Sunnyvale, California, to CommonWealth Partners, LLC. The transaction, which represents the largest single-asset investment office sale in Silicon Valley history, involved Meta Platforms, Inc. as the long-term tenant. Steven Golubchik and his team at Newmark facilitated the deal, highlighting continued investor demand for prime assets in high-barrier-to-entry markets and the strong performance of Moffett Park.

feed.title: Meet Naima Greenwood | President & Chief Operating Officer, Yardstick Management
feed.summary: The article features an interview with Naima Greenwood, President & Chief Operating Officer of Yardstick Management, the nation's leading Black-owned management consulting firm. Greenwood discusses the firm's significant impact on diversity, equity, and inclusion within global organizations like Amazon and Netflix, and their commitment to leveling the playing field for marginalized communities. She also shares personal insights about Atlanta, where Yardstick Management is headquartered, and highlights the important community work of the Villages of Carver YMCA.

feed.title: Walmart enters shoppable TV via exclusive deal with Roku
feed.summary: Walmart has partnered with Roku to introduce shoppable TV, allowing customers to purchase products directly through their Roku remotes while streaming. This collaboration aims to simplify the shopping experience on the largest screen in the home and integrates with Roku Pay for seamless checkout. This initiative is part of Walmart's broader strategy to expand its livestream shopping efforts across various digital platforms.

feed.title: A closer look at P&G’s ‘water positive’ pledge
feed.summary: Procter & Gamble has announced a "water positive" goal by 2030, aiming to restore more water than its operations and products consume. The initiative includes two new restoration pledges focusing on water consumed during manufacturing and by household product use in 18 water-stressed regions, primarily Los Angeles and Mexico City. P&G is investing in various restoration projects and integrating sustainability metrics into executive compensation, while experts commend the company's rigorous approach to consumer-use impact but call for more engagement with public policy for broader impact.

feed.title: DOJ Files Lawsuit Against Meta and Outlines Proposed Settlement Structure Over Allegedly Discriminatory Housing Advertising Practices
feed.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed a lawsuit and a proposed settlement framework against Meta Platforms, Inc. (formerly Facebook) over allegations that Meta's advertising algorithms for housing ads discriminate based on protected characteristics like race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, and national origin, violating the Fair Housing Act. The lawsuit claims Meta used tools like "Lookalike Audience" that considered protected characteristics and that its ad delivery system relied on machine-learning algorithms incorporating these characteristics. The proposed settlement requires Meta to cease using certain tools, develop a new non-discriminatory system by December 2022, implement an independent reviewer, and pay a $115,054 civil penalty.

feed.title: 7 Top Metaverse Stocks with Massive Potential
feed.summary: The metaverse market is projected to reach $5 trillion by 2030, with a significant majority of consumers and industry leaders anticipating positive impacts. This article highlights seven top metaverse stocks and ETFs, including Global X Metaverse ETF (VR), ProShares Metaverse ETF (VERS), Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV), Meta Platforms (META), Nvidia (NVDA), Roblox (RBLX), and Unity Software (U), recommending them as key investment opportunities in this emerging sector. It notes that many of these stocks are currently oversold, presenting potential for future gains as the metaverse concept gains traction.

feed.title: Disney, other U.S. companies offer abortion travel benefit after Roe decision
feed.summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous U.S. companies, including Walt Disney Co. and Meta Platforms Inc., announced they would cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortion services. This move comes as many states are expected to restrict or ban abortions, making it necessary for employees to travel to states where the procedure remains legal. Companies like Dick's Sporting Goods, Lyft, Yelp, Microsoft, Tesla, Apple, Alaska Air Group, Johnson & Johnson, OkCupid, Bumble, Netflix, and JPMorgan Chase & Co. are also offering similar benefits or legal protections.

feed.title: Abortion assistance: Kroger to offer up to $4,000 of out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion
feed.summary: Kroger announced it will offer up to $4,000 to cover out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion and fertility treatments, following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade. The company, headquartered in Cincinnati, operates stores in states like Ohio and Kentucky where abortion is now banned or mostly banned. This move aligns Kroger with nearly two dozen other major U.S. companies providing similar assistance.

feed.title: Lawsuit claims Facebook wrongly collects patient data through health system, hospital websites
feed.summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that Facebook, via its parent company Meta Platforms Inc., wrongly collected sensitive patient data from at least 664 hospital systems and medical provider websites using its Pixel tracking tool. The lawsuit claims that this data, including patient communications, was redirected to Facebook and used for targeted advertising, breaching contract, invading privacy, and violating federal and state privacy laws. This legal action follows a news report revealing that numerous hospital websites were found to be using the Meta Pixel, potentially without proper patient consent or adherence to HIPAA regulations.

feed.title: The “Real State” of the Metaverse in Real Estate
feed.summary: The article explores the growing intersection of the metaverse and real estate, highlighting how companies are investing in virtual land. It discusses the various tax implications associated with buying and selling virtual property and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) using cryptocurrency. The piece also advises potential investors on key considerations such as understanding underlying technology, researching platforms, and learning the acquisition process in the metaverse.

feed.title: Ukraine round-up: Russia leaves Snake Island and Putin's topless G7 comments
feed.summary: Ukraine is celebrating a significant victory as Russian troops withdrew from Snake Island after months of bombardment, though Russia claims it was a "gesture of goodwill." US intelligence agencies believe Russia still aims to take all of Ukraine, but combat has weakened their capacity, suggesting a prolonged conflict. Meanwhile, former F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone sparked controversy with pro-Putin comments, and Western leaders mocked Putin's macho image at the G7 summit.
